heading: Everyday Wellbeing
intro: Wellbeing isn't the absence of difficulty — it's having the understanding, the habits and the support to meet difficulty well. Alongside clinical therapy, I work with individuals, groups and organisations on the foundations that keep mental health steady.
body:
Most people come to therapy at the point where something has become hard to carry. Wellbeing work sits earlier than that. It is preventative rather than remedial: building self-awareness, learning to recognise your own early warning signs, and putting sustainable habits in place before a difficult period becomes a crisis.

That doesn't make it lightweight. The same psychodynamic and trauma-informed thinking that underpins my clinical practice shapes this work too — it is simply applied to everyday life rather than to a presenting difficulty.

Wellbeing sessions are not a substitute for therapy, and I will say so plainly if what you describe would be better served by clinical support. Where that is the case, we can talk about counselling instead.

cards.title: One-to-One Sessions
cards.description: Structured, confidential sessions focused on self-awareness, stress, boundaries and sustainable habits — for people who aren't looking for open-ended therapy but do want dedicated space to think.

cards.title: Group Workshops
cards.description: Facilitated sessions for teams, community groups and organisations, covering the practical side of mental health: recognising pressure, managing stress, and having supportive conversations.

cards.title: Advocacy & Consultancy
cards.description: Advising organisations on how to build wellbeing into the way they actually work — policy, culture, and the everyday practices that make the difference.

faqs.question: Is this the same as counselling?
faqs.answer: No. Counselling and psychotherapy are clinical work — usually weekly, often open-ended, and aimed at understanding and working through difficulty. Wellbeing sessions are shorter-term and more practical, focused on prevention and everyday resilience. If we begin wellbeing work and it becomes clear that therapy would serve you better, I will tell you.

faqs.question: Do I need a referral?
faqs.answer: No. You can get in touch directly, and we will start with a free 20-minute conversation to work out what would help.

faqs.question: Can my employer arrange this?
faqs.answer: Yes — much of my wellbeing work is commissioned by organisations for their teams. Anything discussed in a one-to-one session stays confidential; the organisation receives no detail about individuals.

faqs.question: Is it available online?
faqs.answer: Yes. Both one-to-one sessions and group workshops can run on private video platforms, which for many people makes them far easier to fit around work.

ctaText: A free 20-minute conversation costs nothing and commits you to nothing. We can talk through what you're looking for, and whether wellbeing work or therapy would suit you better.
